newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen president urges citizens to vote in poll.
newsitem.headline: Yemen president urges citizens to vote in poll.

text.p: Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh on Wednesday urged citizens to vote in the country's April 27 parliamentary poll, the first since a 1994 civil war nearly broke the Arab state apart.
"I renew my call to the citizens to be keen and use their right to vote," Saleh said in a speech broadcast by the official media. "It is a national responsibility and duty."
Candidates are campaigning for 301 parliamentary seats under the banners of 12 parties or as independents.

The main opposition Yemen Socialist Party, some of whose former leaders launched the southern separatist campaign that sparked the war, and four others have announced they will boycott the poll because of alleged irregularities.
"The results of the elections will have an impact on your lives and standard of living, on political and social life," Saleh said. "Therefore we call on you to practice your right (to vote)".
Some 4.6 million of the 7.5 million people aged 18 and over who are eligible to vote out of a population of 16 million had registered for the poll when the process ended last August.
Saleh has invited international observers to monitor the poll, and the first group arrived in Yemen earlier this month.
